title: Feature-flagged SDK rollout primer and checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a working primer for shipping SDK surface changes behind a feature flag and running a staged rollout (dev -> dogfood -> beta -> GA). Goal is to minimize friction for integrators, maintain backward compatibility, and capture clear telemetry to gate GA.

Intended audience:
- SDK engineers owning the change
- Solutions / developer advocates running dogfood and pilot customers
- Product PM for launch gating
- SDK docs writer and QA

TL;DR checklist (high level):
- [ ] Define flag semantics and default (server-side flag + client opt-in)
- [ ] Add telemetry contract & event names (see telemetry section)
- [ ] Implement safe defaults and compatibility layer (no breaking change when flag off)
- [ ] Create dogfood build and run 2 internal apps for 1 week
- [ ] Beta: onboard 2–3 pilot customers (opt-in) and measure gating metrics
- [ ] GA only if quality & latency SLOs met and no major regressions

Background and motivation:
We frequently ship new SDK ergonomics (new API, helper wrappers, or network changes). Previous rollouts that were unflagged resulted in friction (integration breakage, unobserved error modes). A feature-flagged rollout buys time to test, iterate, and gather real usage telemetry while keeping the default path stable.

Flag design decisions (recommendations):
- Server-controlled boolean flag with SDK-side safe fallback. Default: OFF.
- Client may opt-in via environment, explicit enable call, or per-request opt header.
- Flag TTL: short (30s) to ensure changes can be turned off fast during incidents.
- Expose flag provenance in SDK logs (flag=on|off, source=server|local).

SDK changes to gate behind the flag (example):
- New streaming chunking behavior (smaller initial chunk, then adaptive)
- New higher-level helper: generateBatchResponses(params) wrapper
- New telemetry enrichment fields (sampled user agent, client version)

Compatibility strategy:
- Provide wrapper functions that check flag and route to old implementation when off.
- Add deprecation runtime warnings only in dev builds (no noisy logs for GA customers).
- Maintain wire-level compatibility: protocol/JSON shape stays compatible when flag off.

Telemetry contract (must be implemented before beta):
- Events (names): sdk.flag.toggled, sdk.feature.invoked, sdk.feature.error, sdk.feature.latency
- Required fields (every event): event_time, sdk_version, flag_state, client_id (hashed), route, latency_ms (if applicable), sample_rate
- Error taxonomy: include error_code (enum), retryable (bool), upstream (bool)
- Sample rate: start at 100% for internal dogfood; 5–10% for beta customer fleets unless pilot says otherwise.
- Storage/links: events should land in the existing telemetry pipeline and be queryable by tag `feature_rollout/<flag-name>`.

Gating metrics (examples to check before GA):
- Functional correctness: error_rate (sdk.feature.error) < 0.5% over 24h on beta traffic
- Latency: p95 latency with flag ON <= baseline p95 * 1.15
- Cost: token-related cost per request not > baseline * 1.25 (if change affects tokenization/overhead)
- Crash rate: native SDK crashes or process exits == baseline
- UX regressions: no increase in user-reported critical issues in pilot Slack/Support channel

Rollout stages and acceptance criteria:
1) Local dev + feature branch
   - Unit tests for both code paths
   - Toggle local flag via env var (DEV_SDK_FLAG=1)
2) Internal dogfood (2–7 days)
   - Build dogfood SDK artifact and deploy to 2 internal services (Console dev, Playground)
   - Telemetry: 100% sampling, check errors & latency daily
   - Accept if no new critical bugs and p95 < threshold
3) Beta (2–4 weeks, opt-in customers)
   - Invite 2–3 pilot customers or internal teams outside SDK
   - Sample rate 5–10%, increase if signals look healthy
   - Run scripted regression suite and capture results
   - Accept if gating metrics met and pilot feedback is positive
4) Gradual GA
   - Canary: 1% of new non-beta customers get the GA change (if server opt-in is used), monitor 24–72h
   - Ramp to 10% -> 50% -> 100% over days with automated checks at each step

Rollback plan:
- Immediate toggle-off server-side; SDK must handle toggle-off gracefully mid-request (return to old behavior for new calls).
- Postmortem runbook: capture last 1h of telemetry, list of pilot customers affected, timeline of events.
- Hotfix plan: if toggle-off insufficient, ship emergency patch (JIRA-EMERGENCY template).

Developer experience / docs deliverables (pre-beta):
- Quickstart snippet (README): how to opt-in and sample code (see sample below)
- Migration guide: mapping old API -> new API with examples and recommended patterns
- Troubleshooting section: common errors and how to read telemetry event fields
- Changelog entry and “breaking changes” checkbox for PM review (even if default OFF)

Sample quickstart snippet (JS):

// opt-in at initialization
const client = new RedwoodSDK({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, featureFlags: { newChunking: true } });
const resp = await client.generate({ prompt: 'hi' });

// opt-in per request
const resp2 = await client.generate({ prompt: 'x', flags: { newChunking: true } });

Notes: keep examples minimal and show how to turn flag off.

PR checklist for SDK owners:
- [ ] Unit + integration tests for both code paths
- [ ] Telemetry events instrumented and validated locally (use test probe)
- [ ] Documentation drafts (quickstart + migration guide) attached to PR
- [ ] Release notes entry stub created
- [ ] Performance bench showing p95 vs baseline attached
- [ ] Security review (if change touches auth or secrets flows)

Pilot coordination template (for Solutions / customer success):
- Outreach email copy (opt-in invite)
- Pilot success criteria (NPS feedback, error rates, latency, feature usage)
- Weekly checkpoint cadence and contact list

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should server-only flags allow roll forward (force-enable) for GA partner requests? (Decide by PM)
- Sampling strategy for telemetry on high-volume customers needs floor and cap (ask SRE)
- Does this change require an SDK minor version bump or patch with opt-in? (semver discussion)

Links / references:
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/987
- Jira epic: JIRA-3412
- Dogfood app list (internal): slack:#dogfood-rollouts

Next actions (owner: Aisha):
- Finalize telemetry event schema with Priya by 2025-01-17
- Wire up server-side flag toggle endpoint (infra ticket JIRA-3419)
- Create dogfood artifact and assign Ethan to deploy to Console dev by 2025-01-22

Notes to self:
- Keep logs quiet for GA customers; dev verbosity only in dev builds
- Keep migration examples short; link to full codelab in docs site

-- end of draft --
